claims.text: Enhanced grain-boundary solute segregation governs high-temperature plastic strain and toughness in fusion plasma-facing structural alloys.
Solute segregation increases grain-boundary cohesion by enhancing local atomic bonding.
Increased grain-boundary cohesion hinders grain-boundary sliding.
Increased grain-boundary cohesion delays initiation and propagation of intergranular cracks.
Grain boundaries can affect deformation behavior and mechanical properties in high-entropy alloys.
Grain-boundary segregation modifies the local atomic structure and cohesion of grain boundaries.
Suppressing grain-boundary-mediated deformation produces a more uniform distribution of plastic strain through controlled dislocation emission and interaction at grain boundaries.
The proposed change in deformation mechanism improves high-temperature toughness.
Fusion reactor plasma-facing materials experience high-temperature, neutron-flux, and severe steady-state or transient thermal-load conditions.
The relevant fusion plasma-facing operating range extends from several hundred degrees Celsius to over 1000 degrees Celsius.
Tungsten alloys and reduced-activation high-entropy steels are representative fusion plasma-facing structural alloys for this hypothesis.
Samples with enhanced segregation will have a higher threshold for grain-boundary sliding than baseline samples.
Samples with enhanced segregation will delay intergranular crack initiation relative to baseline samples.
Samples with enhanced segregation will exhibit greater high-temperature toughness and plastic-strain capacity than unperturbed samples.
The hypothesis is restricted to regimes in which grain-boundary processes dominate high-temperature deformation and precipitation or irradiation damage is not controlling.
The magnitude of the mechanical improvement may depend on alloy system and achieved segregation level.

A comparison of otherwise identical specimens differing in grain-boundary segregation can isolate the hypothesized causal contribution if grain size, precipitates, bulk composition, and testing conditions are held constant.
Failure to improve toughness or plastic-strain capacity and failure to delay grain-boundary sliding or cracking relative to the control would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
